solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Pop a question, somewhat unclear (6)

indicatorNotes.somewhat: only some of the letters of 'Pop a question' are used, a run from inside it

annotation.surface: Someone asks a question that turns out to be rather vague.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pop a question' suggests a proposal of marriage; it is just the text that hides the answer, and 'somewhat' shows only part is taken.
annotation.definitionFit: Opaque writing or thinking is hard to see through, so unclear.

entries.clue: Risk connected with entering border from the south (5)

indicatorNotes.entering: to enter is to go into something, so RE goes inside LIP
indicatorNotes.from the south: in a down entry, read from the bottom, so the letters run upward

blocks.note: a lip is an edge or border

annotation.surface: A danger linked to crossing a frontier from the south.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Border from the south' sounds like a frontier crossing, but in a down entry the south is the bottom, so the letters are read upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: peril is danger or risk.

entries.clue: After two pints, spot rear of venue for hard rock (9)

indicatorNotes.rear of: the rear of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: a zit is a spot on the skin

annotation.surface: Two pints in, someone spots the back of a venue that plays hard rock music.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hard rock' reads as the music, fitting pints and a venue; it is a literal hard rock. The puzzle has a rock-music theme running through it.
annotation.definitionFit: Quartzite is a very hard metamorphic rock formed from sandstone.

entries.clue: Clip from One Direction for spring festival (6)

indicatorNotes.Clip: to clip is to trim, so the word loses its tail

blocks.note: a compass direction as an adjective, with its last letter clipped off

annotation.surface: A video clip from the boy band One Direction for a spring celebration.
annotation.walkthrough: One Direction is a pop boy band, and 'clip' suggests a video; here 'one direction' is simply EASTERN, trimmed to lose its N.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Christian feast of the Resurrection falls in spring, on a date that moves with the moon.

entries.clue: Referencing, in report, something from The Observer? (8)

indicatorNotes.in report: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

annotation.surface: A newspaper item citing a story from The Observer.
annotation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper, which fits 'report' and 'referencing'; here it is anyone who observes, and a sighting is what they come up with.
annotation.definitionFit: An observer's product is a sighting, something seen; the question mark flags the newspaper pun.

entries.clue: Single women afflicted with heatstroke (5,2,3,5)

indicatorNotes.afflicted: afflicted letters are troubled and disordered, so they are rearranged

annotation.surface: Unmarried women suffering in a heatwave.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Single' looks like it describes the women; it is the definition, a record released as a single. Smoke on the Water is the Deep Purple hard-rock hit.
annotation.definitionFit: Smoke on the Water was released as a single by Deep Purple in 1973.

entries.clue: Get stuck in dress worn by Dorothy’s companion (2,2,4)

indicatorNotes.worn by: GOWN wears TOTO, holding it inside

blocks.note: Toto is Dorothy's dog in The Wizard of Oz

annotation.surface: A dress that gets snagged on Dorothy's little dog.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get stuck in' suggests being snagged or trapped, but it means doing something with gusto.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom match: both phrases mean throwing yourself into something with enthusiasm and no restraint.

entries.clue: What may go with nail — biter? (5)

blocks.note: the partner of 'nail' in a set phrase for fighting fiercely
a part of the mouth that does the biting

annotation.surface: A nail-biter, split by a dash into a question.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash breaks 'nail-biter' in two: one half is the phrase 'tooth and nail', the other a thing that bites.
annotation.definitionFit: Tooth pairs with nail in 'tooth and nail', and a tooth is literally a biter.

entries.clue: Close call when new channel ultimately rejected by terrestrial (4,5)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: the ultimate, final letter of 'channel' is L
indicatorNotes.rejected by: L is thrown out of EARTHLING

blocks.note: EARTHLING, a terrestrial being, without the L

annotation.surface: A narrow escape as a new TV channel is dropped by the terrestrial broadcasters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Terrestrial' suggests broadcast TV, fitting 'channel'; here it is a noun, an inhabitant of Earth.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both phrases describe an outcome that was only just avoided.

entries.clue: Burns possibly to the ear? Blimey! (5,5)

indicatorNotes.to the ear: what reaches the ear is the sound, not the spelling

blocks.note: Robert Burns, the national poet, is a great Scot

annotation.surface: Someone exclaims on hearing about burns, perhaps from a fire.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Burns' capitalised at the start of the clue could be injuries; it is Robert Burns, Scotland's national poet.
annotation.definitionFit: Great Scott! and Blimey! are both exclamations of surprise.

entries.clue: Staff follows how oenophile opens Muscat here (4)

indicatorNotes.opens: the letter that opens 'oenophile' is its first
indicatorNotes.follows: to follow is to come behind, so the word for 'staff' is placed after O

blocks.note: to staff a post is to man it

annotation.surface: A wine lover uncorks a bottle of Muscat, the grape.
annotation.walkthrough: Muscat is a sweet grape and wine, fitting the oenophile (wine lover); here it is the capital city of Oman.
annotation.definitionFit: Muscat is the capital of Oman, so Oman is where Muscat is found.

entries.clue: Sound of locksmith initially cutting key at this location (3,5)

indicatorNotes.initially: only the initial letter of 'locksmith' is used
indicatorNotes.cutting: L cuts into ALT, sitting inside it

blocks.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

annotation.surface: A locksmith cutting a key on the spot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like noise, which suits a lock; it means mentally sound. The key is a keyboard key, not a door key.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who is all there is mentally sound, with their wits about them.

entries.clue: Island nation’s leader moving right on time (6)

indicatorNotes.moving right: H, the leader, moves one step to the right, so HAITI becomes AHITI
indicatorNotes.on: in an across entry, one thing on another is placed after it, so the shifted nation follows T

blocks.note: HAITI with its first letter H shifted one place right

annotation.surface: An island country's president shifting politically to the right, just in time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Island nation' reads as one phrase, but the nation is Haiti and the island is the definition. 'Leader moving right' sounds political; it moves a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Tahiti is an island in French Polynesia in the Pacific.

entries.clue: Charge one vehicle with meter (4)

blocks.note: a charge levied by the government

annotation.surface: A fee levied on a single vehicle fitted with a meter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charge' fits the fare on a meter, which is part of the definition's picture; here it is a levy.
annotation.definitionFit: A taxi is a hired car whose fare is shown on a meter.

entries.clue: Vegetable — with skill I bottle it (9)

blocks.note: to bottle it is to lose your nerve, to choke

annotation.surface: A cook confesses that, for all their skill, they make a mess of preserving vegetables in jars.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bottle it' suggests preserving vegetables in jars; it is British slang for losing your nerve.
annotation.definitionFit: The artichoke is a thistle-like plant whose flower head is eaten as a vegetable.

entries.clue: Former colony is the latest source of irritation (3,5)

blocks.note: the news is the latest information

annotation.surface: A complaint that a former colony is the newest thing to cause annoyance.
annotation.walkthrough: The obvious split is NEW and a country, but the wordplay divides after the S, so the country is never clued directly.
annotation.definitionFit: New Spain was the Spanish colonial viceroyalty centred on Mexico.

entries.clue: Wine mixed in iron pot (5,4)

indicatorNotes.mixed: the letters are mixed up into a new order

annotation.surface: Wine being stirred together in an iron cooking pot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like the link between wine and pot; it is part of the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the red Burgundy grape gives its name to the wine made from it.

entries.clue: Fights off policeman after losing head in present location? (4,4)

indicatorNotes.off: letters that are off are out of order, so FIGHTS is rearranged
indicatorNotes.after: OP comes after the rearranged letters

annotation.surface: Someone fending off a policeman after losing their temper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fights off' reads as repelling an attacker; 'off' is the anagram signal. 'Present' means a gift, not the current place.
annotation.definitionFit: A gift shop is where presents are sold; the question mark flags the pun on 'present location'.

entries.clue: The spies go flying rather high (8)

indicatorNotes.go flying: letters sent flying land in a new order

annotation.surface: Spies taking to the air at a fair altitude.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rather high' seems to say how high the spies fly; it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Steepish means somewhat steep, fairly high, as of a price or slope.

entries.clue: Board member undressed nearby (4)

indicatorNotes.undressed: stripped of its outer covering, the first and last letters

blocks.note: KNIGHT, a chess piece, without K and T

annotation.surface: A company director stripped naked close at hand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Board member' suggests a company director; the board is a chessboard and the member a knight.
annotation.definitionFit: Nigh is an old word for near, close by.

entries.clue: Dated northern town losing last plant in the end (3,3)

indicatorNotes.in the end: only the end letter of 'plant' is used

annotation.surface: A dated northern mill town that has lost its last factory.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a factory, fitting a declining northern town; only its last letter is used. Oldham is a town near Manchester in northern England.
annotation.definitionFit: Something old hat is out of date and unfashionable.

entries.clue: Exonerate half of rock band then leave (6)

blocks.note: half of AC/DC, the hard-rock band

annotation.surface: Half a band is cleared of wrongdoing and then walks out.
annotation.walkthrough: The rock band is AC/DC, whose name splits neatly in half; it fits the puzzle's rock theme.
annotation.definitionFit: To acquit is to clear someone of a charge, to exonerate them.

entries.clue: Overturn winning goal (5)

blocks.note: a team that is up is ahead, winning
an end is an aim or goal

annotation.surface: A late winning goal turns a match on its head.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Goal' suggests football; it is an end in the sense of an aim.
annotation.definitionFit: To upend something is to turn it upside down, to overturn it.

entries.clue: Having lots of money is boring at the beginning, outstanding at the end (4-2-2)

blocks.note: a well is made by boring into the ground
work still outstanding is still to do

annotation.surface: Being rich is dull at first but excellent in the end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boring' and 'outstanding' read as dull and excellent; they mean drilling and not yet done. 'At the beginning' and 'at the end' only place the two parts.
annotation.definitionFit: Well-to-do means wealthy, having plenty of money.

entries.clue: House in Russia — yes, in Russia — man left unfinished (5)

indicatorNotes.left unfinished: CHAP is left without its final letter

annotation.surface: A Russian saying yes, and a man walking out before the job is done.
annotation.walkthrough: The repeated 'in Russia' belongs once to the definition and once to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian country house or cottage.

entries.clue: Jack trimmed roses? No way man! (4)

indicatorNotes.trimmed: ROSES is trimmed at both ends

blocks.note: ROSES without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: Someone refusing outright when asked to prune the roses.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the man in the saying 'No way, José!'. 'Jack' could be a man's name too; here it is the playing card.
annotation.definitionFit: José is the man named in the retort 'No way, José!'

entries.clue: Mix stew outside one church then another (10)

indicatorNotes.outside: the stew goes outside the church, wrapped around it on both sides
indicatorNotes.then: 'then' means next in order, so another church is added at the end

blocks.note: a hotpot is a meat stew

annotation.surface: A cook stirring stew outside one church and then another.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mix' reads as a verb for stirring the stew; it is a noun, a jumble. A hotpot is a Lancashire stew of meat under sliced potatoes.
annotation.definitionFit: A hotchpotch is a confused mixture of things.

entries.clue: Mineral, one extracted from meadow, placed by box (8)

indicatorNotes.extracted from: to extract is to pull out, as a tooth is extracted, so I is removed from the meadow word
indicatorNotes.placed by: SPAR is placed next to FELD

annotation.surface: A mineral dug out of a meadow and set down beside a box.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a container; it is the verb to fight with fists.
annotation.definitionFit: Feldspar is the commonest group of rock-forming minerals.

entries.clue: Sailor meets endlessly eccentric swinger in the woods (6)

annotation.surface: A sailor runs into an oddball swinging through the trees.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swinger' hints at a party-goer; it is Tarzan swinging on jungle vines.
annotation.definitionFit: Tarzan, the jungle hero, swings from tree to tree on vines.
